We use the notation of the main text. The spatial lattice is the one-dimensional qubit lattice Z, with local algebras A{x} ≃ Mat2(C), AΩ = O y∈Ω A{y} for every finite region Ω ⋐ Z. In the notation {y}r, the first entry denotes the spatial site and the second entry the instrument layer. Thus {y}r is a layer-labelled copy of the site y; the associated local algebra remains A{y}. For a single Kraus operator K, we write Ad[K](A) := K† AK for the corresponding Heisenberg operation.
